3f1f99d3-ebcb-50c6-a162-bd58f7d5ec92.title: Listing the Elements in a Power Set

e-13199.knowledge_point: Listing the Elements in a Power Set
e-13199.worked_solution:
The power set of $A,$ denoted $\mathcal{P}(A),$ is the set that contains every possible subset of $A,$ including the empty set $\emptyset.$

So, let's list all possible subsets of $A$ using a tree diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14095809/assets/b3af256806e0aeb0396564320800f908c66d5830ab46e676dfc51ceab24154f6.png)

According to our diagram, the subsets of $A$ are

$$
\emptyset = \{\},\quad \{2\},\quad \{4\},\quad \{ \{8\} \}, \quad \{2, 4\},\quad \{2, \{8\}\},\quad \{4, \{8\}\},\quad\{2, 4, \{8\}\}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\mathcal{P}(A) = \{\emptyset, \{2\}, \{4\}, \{\{8\}\}, \{2, 4\}, \{2, \{8\}\}, \{4, \{8\}\},\{2, 4, \{8\}\}\}.
$$

decision.explanation: The power set contains all 2^3 = 8 subsets: the empty set, three singletons, three pairs, and T itself. Option a lists all eight.
